title: Practical Learning Activities
intro: Skills develop by doing. These nine beginner-friendly activities build from identification to inspection to record keeping. Where the activity involves a real vehicle, it must be done under qualified supervision with the safety steps from Chapter 5.
objectives: Carry out guided visual inspections of pads, discs, drums and fluid.
Complete an inspection checklist and record findings.

blocks.warn: Activities that involve lifting a vehicle or removing wheels must be done under qualified supervision, with the vehicle correctly lifted, supported on stands and chocked. If you do not have access to a vehicle, use photographs, a training brake assembly or a parts display.

activity.title: Activity 1: Identifying brake components
activity.objective: Name the main parts of a disc brake, drum brake and hydraulic system, and state the purpose of each.
tools: Diagrams or photographs from this guide
Optional: a brake display board or removed parts
safety: Handle any real parts carefully; edges can be sharp.
Wash your hands after handling used parts.
procedure: Study the labelled diagrams for five minutes.
Hide the labels, and name every part you can from memory.
For each part, write one sentence on its purpose.
Check your answers against the table, and correct them.
Repeat for any parts you missed.
activity.expected: You can name at least 15 components and explain their purpose.
mistakes: Confusing the pad with the shoe.
Confusing the caliper with the wheel cylinder.
Forgetting the booster and the reservoir.
activity.assessment: Cover the table and name the parts that belong to a disc brake, a drum brake and the hydraulic system without help. Aim for 90% correct.

activity.title: Activity 2: Identifying automotive tools
activity.objective: Recognise the tools in Chapter 4 and describe the purpose and safety precautions of each.
tools: Tool photographs or a tool board
safety: Do not use any tool unless you know how to do so safely.
Check tools for damage before use.
procedure: Lay out or view the tools.
Name each tool.
State its purpose and one safety precaution.
Match the correct tool to each of these tasks: loosening a wheel nut, setting a torque, reading rotor thickness, supporting a raised vehicle.
Review any you missed.
activity.expected: You can identify all 16 tools and match the correct tool to a task.
mistakes: Using a jack as a support.
Using a torque wrench to loosen a fastener.
Confusing a micrometer and a vernier caliper.
activity.assessment: Explain to a partner why jack stands are used in addition to the jack.

activity.title: Activity 3: Inspecting brake pads
activity.objective: Carry out a guided visual and measured inspection of brake pads and record the findings.
materials: Service manual specification for the vehicle
safety: Complete the Workshop Safety Checklist.
Do not use compressed air to remove dust.
Allow parts to cool before touching.
procedure: Lift, support and chock the vehicle with a supervisor.
Remove the wheel in the specified sequence.
Observe the inner and outer pads.
Measure the friction material thickness.
Compare to the manual minimum and compare sides.
Check for glazing, cracks and contamination.
Record the findings. Refit the wheel to specification under supervision.
activity.expected: A completed record showing thickness for both pads, wear pattern and your conclusion about the next action.
mistakes: Measuring the backing plate with the friction material.
Forgetting to compare inner and outer pads.
Not referring to the manual minimum.
activity.assessment: Explain why uneven wear between inner and outer pads suggests a problem in the caliper rather than just worn pads.

activity.title: Activity 4: Inspecting brake discs
activity.objective: Inspect a rotor for wear and damage and measure its thickness and runout.
safety: Rotors can be sharp at the edge or hot.
Secure the rotor correctly before measuring runout.
procedure: Clean the rotor surface carefully with a dust-safe method.
Inspect both faces for scoring, cracks, heat marks and rust.
Feel the edge for a ridge.
Measure thickness at several points around the disc.
Measure runout with a dial indicator.
Compare to the manual's limits and record.
activity.expected: Recorded thickness at multiple points, runout value and a decision to keep, resurface or replace.
mistakes: Measuring in only one place.
Not zeroing the dial indicator.
Ignoring a rust lip at the edge.
activity.assessment: State how a rotor that is below minimum thickness should be treated.

activity.title: Activity 5: Inspecting brake drums
activity.objective: Inspect a drum and shoes and measure the drum diameter.
tools: Brake spring pliers if the shoes are to be examined closely (supervised)
safety: Springs may release suddenly. Wear eye protection.
Do not breathe the dust.
procedure: Remove the drum as the manual directs.
Inspect the drum surface for scoring and cracks.
Measure the inside diameter at several places.
Inspect shoes, springs, adjuster and wheel cylinder.
Record findings and compare to the manual.
activity.expected: A completed Drum Brake Inspection checklist and recorded measurements.
mistakes: Forgetting to back off the adjuster first.
Not checking the wheel cylinder for leaks.
Touching friction surfaces with greasy hands.
activity.assessment: Explain what fluid on the shoes would indicate and what must be done.

activity.title: Activity 6: Checking brake fluid
activity.objective: Check the level and condition of brake fluid and decide on the next action.
tools: Clear container with fresh fluid for comparison (optional)
safety: Protect painted surfaces.
Wash off any splashes of fluid immediately.
Close the container after use.
procedure: Park on level ground.
Wipe around the reservoir cap.
Read the level against MIN and MAX.
Observe colour and clarity.
Compare with fresh fluid if available.
Record the result and decide: no action, investigate, or replace.
activity.expected: A recorded level and condition with a reasoned recommendation.
mistakes: Opening the cap without cleaning around it.
Topping up without finding out why the level is low.
Using the wrong fluid.
activity.assessment: Explain why old brake fluid affects braking performance.

activity.title: Activity 7: Identifying brake system leaks
activity.objective: Locate typical leak points and tell the difference between brake fluid and other fluids.
materials: Photographs or a vehicle for observation
safety: Never put your hands or face near a suspected pressurised leak.
Do not drive a vehicle you suspect has a brake leak.
procedure: Check the master cylinder and booster area.
Follow the brake lines, checking fittings.
Inspect the hoses at each wheel.
Look at calipers and wheel cylinders.
Wipe suspicious wet areas with a white cloth to see the colour.
Note the position and likely source of each leak.
activity.expected: A list of inspected locations with notes on each, and any suspected sources.
mistakes: Mistaking water or oil for brake fluid.
Looking only at the wheel and ignoring the lines.
Not checking inside the dust boots.
activity.assessment: Explain why any confirmed brake fluid leak means the vehicle should not be driven.

activity.title: Activity 8: Completing a brake inspection checklist
activity.objective: Work through a complete brake inspection using the checklists.
materials: Pre-Maintenance, Visual, Disc/Drum, Fluid, Parking Brake and Final checklists
safety: Follow the whole workshop safety checklist.
Work with a supervisor.
procedure: Complete the Pre-Maintenance checklist.
Complete the Workshop Safety checklist.
Carry out the visual inspection.
Complete the disc or drum checklist for each axle.
Complete the fluid and parking brake checklists.
Complete the Final Inspection checklist.
activity.expected: All relevant checklists are completed with notes.
mistakes: Ticking items without actually checking them.
Skipping the measurements.
Not noting what was compared to.
activity.assessment: Summarise the findings and recommend a next action in two or three sentences.

activity.title: Activity 9: Recording maintenance findings
activity.objective: Write a clear maintenance record that another person could understand and use.
materials: Documentation checklist and table from Chapter 9
safety: Check that all numbers are copied correctly, as an error can cause a wrong decision.
procedure: Record date, vehicle and mileage.
Record the complaint.
Record each measurement with its specification.
List parts replaced and fluid used.
Record the road test result.
Write a short recommendation for the owner.
Ask a supervisor to review and sign.
mistakes: Writing numbers without units.
Forgetting the specification used.
Leaving out recommendations.
activity.assessment: Swap records with a colleague and see if they can understand the vehicle's condition without asking questions.

concepts: Observation first, measurement second, recording always.
Each activity uses the same safety habits.
Supervision is required for work on real vehicles.
examples: A learner finds a thin inner pad and a thicker outer pad on the same caliper and records that the slide pins should be inspected and cleaned.
safety: Do not attempt vehicle activities unsupervised.
practice: Choose any two activities and complete them using photographs, a parts display or a supervised vehicle.

check.q: Why are measurements recorded with their units and specifications?
check.a: So that the reader can check whether they pass or fail, and avoid misreading.

check.q: Which activity trains you to find leaks?
What should you do if you find a brake fluid leak on a vehicle?
check.a: Do not drive it; identify the source and arrange a repair.

summary: Practice builds from identification to measurement to documentation.
All real-vehicle activities require supervision and safety steps.
